description: A team chat with Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity on your own subscriptions: task routing by model and effort, brainstorms, cross-review.
untrusted.description: Agents run commands and edit files in the project, so in Restricted Mode the chat only opens for reading history.
command.openInEditor: Open chat in an editor tab
config.language.auto: Follow the VS Code display language (Russian for Russian, English otherwise).
config.language: Language of the chat interface and of the instructions agents get, so plans and summaries come back in it too. `auto` follows the VS Code display language.
config.agents.claude.path: Path to the claude binary (if it is not on the editor's PATH).
config.agents.claude.chrome: Connect Claude to Chrome through the Claude in Chrome extension (`--chrome`). Claude works in your browser with all your signed-in accounts. In “Read only” mode it can only open and read pages, in “Edits” it clicks and types after an auto-check, in “Full access” without confirmations.
config.team.maxIterations: Team autopilot: how many “plan → tasks → check” iterations the lead may run without the CEO until the goal is reached.
config.team.maxHandoffs: How many times in a row agents may hand the turn to each other by @mention (`@codex, check this`) before Harness stops and waits for the CEO. `0`: mentioning an agent does not pass the turn.
config.telegram.enabled: Mirror the team chat to Telegram and take tasks from there, once a bot is connected (**Harness: Connect Telegram**). Only the chat you link with a one-time code is served; the bot runs while VS Code is open.
config.telegram.apiUrl: Telegram Bot API server. Change it only for a self-hosted Bot API server or a proxy you trust: the bot token is sent there.
config.routing.classifier: How the router assesses the complexity and area of a task.
config.routing.classifier.llm: A cheap model (Haiku / Luna, low effort) assesses the complexity and area of the task; rules pick the assignee.
config.routing.classifier.heuristic: Text heuristics only, no extra calls.
config.routing.affinity: Agent preference order per task area. The first one is the main candidate.
config.models: Which model and effort each complexity level uses. An empty model means the agent's default model.
config.strengths: What each agent is good at: a hint for the router and the lead. Agents not listed here get a built-in description in the interface language.
